rules.statement: The first viewport is the work itself; no headline about craft appears before the thing being shown.
The grid uses one aspect ratio per row and reserves space for every tile, so images arriving never move the layout; at 320 px it becomes a single column in reading order.
Opening an image is a dialog with a visible close, Escape to dismiss, focus trapped and restored to the originating tile; the URL does not change unless the image is shareable.
Outcomes are attributed to a named client and a period, or labelled as illustrative; a case study never implies measured impact it cannot show.
Each tile ships a compressed still under its declared budget with width descriptors, and the largest image is not preloaded unless it is the LCP element.
Alt text describes what the work shows, not the file name or 'image'; purely decorative crops are marked empty rather than described.

stateMachine.staleResponseRule: an opened dialog owns its image request; a response that arrives after the dialog closed is discarded and never reopens the overlay

sections.intent: Show the work at a glance, let someone open any piece to look closely, and state what it did without dressing up the evidence.
useCases: scan a designer's portfolio in twenty seconds
open one project and read the constraint and the outcome
send a specific image link to a colleague
nicheDifferences: Experience surfaces are the artifact, so the interface must recede
Any chrome that competes with the work is a bug, and any claim that outruns the evidence is a lie with good typography
inputs: the images, their aspect ratios, and which is the LCP element
the client names that may be published and the periods involved
which outcomes are measured and which are illustrative
the declared weight budget per tile
anatomy: a tile grid with reserved space
an image dialog with close and next/previous
a case-study body with constraint, decision and outcome
a caption system that separates fact from illustration
styling: the grid rhythm comes from one aspect ratio per row, not from masonry surprise
captions are quiet; the work carries the contrast
the dialog background is near-opaque so the image is the only bright surface
a11y: every tile is a button with an accessible name describing the work
the dialog traps focus, closes on Escape, and returns focus to the tile
alt text describes the work; decorative crops are empty strings
the grid is keyboard-navigable in reading order
responsive: at 320 px the grid is one column in reading order, not a horizontally scrolled strip
the dialog fits the image within 90 vh and 90 vw with the caption still visible
captions never truncate; they wrap under the image
copy: captions name the client, the year and what the image shows
outcomes are stated with their source or labelled 'illustrative'
the dialog offers 'Close' as a visible button, not only an X icon
alternatives: a single long scroll when the work is a sequence
a film or motion piece where the work moves
a downloadable PDF for procurement contexts where print still wins
acceptance: the first viewport shows the work, with no headline above it
tiles reserve space so arriving images do not move the layout
the dialog traps focus, closes on Escape and restores focus to the tile
at 320 px the grid is a single column in reading order
outcomes are attributed or labelled illustrative
failureCases: a masonry grid reflows as images arrive and the reader clicks the wrong piece
the lightbox has no visible close and traps a keyboard user
an outcome is stated as a percentage with no source
decorative crops are described as 'image' in alt text
